Blocked Drains Inner West: Cleared, Camera-Checked and Fixed

Cleared properly, then checked with a camera so you know why it blocked.

A blocked drain is a sewer or waste pipe that can no longer carry water away because something is stuck inside it, usually tree roots, fat, wipes or a broken joint. Our licensed plumbers clear blocked drains across the Inner West, then find and fix the cause so the same drain does not block again next month.

Which drain is blocked? Read the signs

Where the water backs up tells you where the blockage is. One slow sink means a branch pipe. A gurgling toilet when the shower runs, or water rising out of the grate in the yard, means the main sewer line is blocked further down, and that needs a plumber with a jetter and a camera.

1Kitchen sink waste

Fat, oil and food scraps cool and stick to the inside of the pipe. A blocked kitchen sink is usually a build-up a few metres down the line, which is why plungers and drain cleaners rarely shift it for long.

2Shower and floor waste

Hair and soap scum wrap around the grate and trap. If the shower drain is blocked and the toilet gurgles at the same time, the problem is in the main line, not the shower.

3Overflow relief gully

The grated gully in the yard is a safety valve. Its loose grate is meant to pop off so sewage spills outside instead of inside your home. Never seal it or bury it under pavers or pots.

4Inspection opening

A capped riser on the sewer line. It is where we put the jetter and camera in, so we can clear and check the line without lifting a toilet or digging.

5Roots at a clay joint

Old clay pipes come in short lengths with a joint every metre or so. Roots find a hairline crack, grow in for the water and form a mat that catches everything flowing past.

6Point of connection

Where your private sewer meets the Sydney Water junction. Your side, including the joint itself, is yours to maintain. The main and the body of the junction are Sydney Water's.

Blocked drain plumber for every drain in the house

We clear every kind of blocked drain on Inner West homes, shops and strata buildings, from a single slow basin to a sewer line choked with roots under the backyard. You get one blocked drain plumber who can clear it, show you what caused it on camera and fix the pipe if it is damaged.

Blocked sewer lines

A blocked sewer is the main pipe carrying everything from the house to the street. When it chokes, toilets gurgle, the yard gully overflows and every fixture slows down. We clear a blocked sewer pipe from the inspection opening or gully, so there is no need to pull up a toilet first.

Kitchen sinks, showers and floor wastes

Grease in a blocked kitchen sink, or hair in a shower drain that is blocked, sits in branch pipes inside the house. We clear them through the fixture or the nearest access point and check the line beyond, in case the real problem is further down.

Toilets that will not flush away

A toilet that rises and drains slowly is often a sign of a bigger blockage, not the toilet itself. If the pan, cistern or seal is the problem, our toilet repair plumbers sort it on the same visit.

Stormwater pits and downpipes

Leaves, silt and roots block stormwater lines too, and the yard floods every time it rains. That is a separate system from the sewer, and our stormwater plumber page explains how we clear pits, grates and the line to the kerb.

Inner West Sydney Plumbers is a licensed and insured local team with over 20 years clearing blocked drains for homes, businesses and strata buildings.

How we clear a blocked drain

Drain unblocking is only half the job. We find the right access point, clear the line with the tool that suits the pipe, then run a camera through it before we leave, so you see what caused the block and whether the pipe is sound. Nothing beyond the clearing goes ahead without your say-so.

  1. Find the access point

    We open the yard gully or inspection opening rather than working through a toilet or sink.

  2. Clear the line

    Jetter, cable machine or root cutter, matched to the pipe and the blockage.

  3. Camera the pipe

    We run the camera end to end and show you the footage on the screen.

  4. Agree what is next

    If the pipe is cracked or full of roots, you get your options and the price first.

Hydro jetting

Hydro jetting pushes water at high pressure through a hose with a nozzle that fires jets backwards. The jets drive the hose along the pipe and scour fat, silt and soft roots off the walls, leaving the full bore clear rather than a hole punched through the middle. It is our first choice for drain cleaning where grease and silt are the problem.

Cable machines and root cutters

A cable machine, often called an electric eel, spins a steel cable with a cutting head through the pipe. It suits tight branch lines and thick root masses that need cutting before they can be flushed out. Roots cut this way grow back, so we always check the joint they came through.

Camera check before we leave

Clearing tells you the pipe flows. The camera tells you why it blocked. We push a waterproof camera along the line, measure where any crack, root entry or sag sits and mark it on the ground. For a full report before you buy or renovate, book a CCTV drain inspection.

Why do Inner West drains block so often?

Most Inner West streets were built well before plastic pipe existed. Their sewers are still the original clay lines, laid in short lengths with a joint every metre or so, running under narrow backyards beside big trees. Every joint is a way in for roots, and every root mat catches paper, wipes and grease.

Clay pipes with mortar joints

Terraces and Federation homes in suburbs like Marrickville, Leichhardt, Balmain and Ashfield were drained with glazed clay pipe joined with mortar or rubber rings. After a century of ground movement, the joints crack and open. The pipe itself is often still sound, which is why relining or a spot repair can save digging up the whole line.

Terrace rows on one shared line

Some older terrace rows share one private sewer line that runs through several backyards before it reaches the main. A blockage downstream can back up into a neighbour's yard, and the owners connected to that line share responsibility for it. We trace the line on camera so everyone knows where the problem sits.

Big trees on small blocks

Large street trees and backyard figs, palms and gums send roots a long way looking for water, and an old sewer joint is a reliable source. Our guide to tree roots in old clay drains explains how roots get in and what keeps them out for good.

Clear, repair or reline: what does your drain need?

If the pipe is sound and the block was fat, wipes or a few roots, clearing is enough. If the camera shows one broken or sunken section, a spot repair fixes it. If roots are coming in at joint after joint, or the pipe runs under a slab or a tree, relining seals the whole run without digging a trench.

Which option fits is decided from the camera footage, never guessed.
OptionWhen it fitsWhat's involvedDisruptionWhat to expect after

Spot repairOne cracked, collapsed or sunken section in a spot we can reachDig down at the marked spot and replace that length with PVC pipeOne hole, filled and made goodThat section is like new; the rest of the old line stays as it was

A sewer line repair is the right call when one section has failed, and relining is the right call when the problem runs the length of the pipe. We show you the footage and explain which fits, and our pipe relining page covers how the liner goes in and how long it takes.

Who is responsible for a blocked sewer: you, Sydney Water or strata?

You are responsible for the private sewer pipes on your property, up to and including the point where they connect to Sydney Water's system, even if that point sits under the footpath or road. Sydney Water looks after its main and the body of the junction. In a strata building, shared drains are usually common property.

Sydney Water only pays when the fault is confirmed in its own pipes, which is why the camera footage matters. Its page on responsibility for repairs sets out the split. For apartment buildings, our strata plumbing team works with building managers, and our guide on who pays for plumbing in an NSW strata building covers the rules.

What does a blocked drain cost to fix?

The cost depends on where the blockage is, what caused it and how easy the line is to reach, so we price each job once we know what is involved. You will know the price before any work starts, and nothing goes ahead until you say yes. A camera check costs far less than clearing the same drain twice.

For a wider picture of call-out and labour rates, read our guide to what plumbers charge in the Inner West.

  1. Where the blockage isA single basin trap is quicker than a main sewer line under the backyard.
  2. What caused itGrease and wipes flush out; a thick root mat has to be cut, then flushed.
  3. AccessA clear yard gully or inspection opening makes the job faster than working through a toilet.
  4. The state of the pipeA sound pipe only needs clearing; a broken one needs a repair or relining as well.
  5. When you callAfter-hours work can cost more than a weekday booking, and we tell you before we come.

Keeping the drain clear afterwards

Most repeat blockages come from three things: grease down the sink, wipes and sanitary items down the toilet, and roots coming back through a joint that was cleared but never sealed. Small habits deal with the first two. The camera footage tells you whether the third needs a repair.

  • Wipe greasy pans with paper towel and put it in the bin before washing up.
  • Only toilet paper goes down the toilet. Wipes labelled flushable still do not break down in a clay sewer.
  • Keep the grate on the yard gully clear and loose, and never pave or plant over it.
  • Fit a hair catcher in the shower and empty the sink strainer into the bin.
  • If roots were cut, ask us about a maintenance clean before they grow back, or seal the joint for good.

Blocked drain questions from Inner West locals

Straight answers to what people ask when a drain backs up. Anything else, call 0412 395 426 and talk to a plumber.

How quickly can you get to a blocked drain in the Inner West?

Call 0412 395 426 and we will tell you on the phone when a plumber can be there. We are open 24 hours, so a drain that backs up at night or on a weekend still gets an answer. An emergency blocked drain, such as sewage coming up through a floor waste, is handled by our emergency plumber team first.

How much does it cost to unblock a drain?

It depends on where the blockage is, what caused it and how easy the line is to reach. A basin trap is a quick job; a root-choked sewer under the backyard takes longer and may need cutting and a camera check. We tell you the price before any work starts, and nothing goes ahead until you agree to it.

Is hydro jetting safe for old clay pipes?

Yes, for a clay pipe that is intact. Jetting cleans the walls without the scraping of a cable. Where a pipe is already cracked or collapsed, high pressure can make the damage worse, so on older lines we run the camera first and choose the method to suit what we see.

Will Sydney Water pay if the blockage is in their main?

Sydney Water pays when the fault is confirmed in its own pipes, which means the main or the body of the junction. If our camera shows the blockage is there, we stop and report it to Sydney Water so its crew can verify it. Everything on your side of the point of connection is the owner's cost.

Why does my drain keep blocking after it has been cleared?

Usually because the cause is still there. Roots that were cut grow back through the same cracked joint, a sagging section of pipe holds water and silt, or grease keeps going down the sink. A camera inspection shows which one it is, and that decides whether you need maintenance clearing, a repair or relining.

What happens if the drain blocks again after you clear it?

Call us and tell us when it was last cleared. Before we leave any job we show you the camera footage and tell you plainly if the pipe has open joints or roots that will come back. If it blocks again, that footage tells us straight away whether it is the same fault and what will fix it properly.

Will you need to dig up my yard or courtyard?

Not to clear a drain. We work through the yard gully or an inspection opening. Digging only comes up when the camera finds a collapsed or broken section that has to be replaced, and even then relining can often avoid a trench under pavers, a slab or a tree. We explain the options before anything is lifted.

Do you clear drains for strata buildings, shops and restaurants?

Yes. We work with owners corporations, building managers and businesses as well as homes, from shared sewer lines in apartment blocks to grease-heavy kitchen drains in cafes. Our commercial plumber team can work early or late to keep a shop trading.

Do you cover my suburb?

We clear blocked drains right across the Inner West, Canada Bay, Burwood and Strathfield council areas, from Balmain and Drummoyne to Marrickville, Dulwich Hill and Homebush. Check every Inner West suburb we cover, or call and tell us your street.

OPEN 24 HOURS

Day or night, every day of the year.

Drain backing up right now?

Water rising out of the yard gully or a toilet that will not go down will not fix itself. Call now, or pick what is happening and we will ring you back.
